title: Excalibur — Markdown-Configured Agent Framework
description: Opinionated framework for building AI agent systems configured entirely through markdown files. Primitives include charge management (per-operation token budgeting), tiered memory layers (working to archive), security boundaries (shared vs internal surfaces), and scheduled rituals (autonomous workflows). No code — markdown guidelines only. The charge/budgeting system for tracking token cost per operation is potentially novel; the rest overlaps with existing agent architecture. Needs evaluation for IMPROVEMENT vs DUPLICATE classification. Discovered via Discord #general 2026-04-03.

evaluation.reasoning: Mixed DUPLICATE/IMPROVEMENT classification. Most primitives map directly to existing capabilities: tiered memory layers → agent-event-bus + CLAUDE.md hierarchy; security boundaries → Agent Spawn Restrictions; scheduled rituals → cron heartbeat system; markdown-only configuration → existing skills/agents pattern. The one potentially novel concept is 'charge management' — per-operation token budgeting as an explicit resource tracked alongside work. This is architecturally distinct from our token efficiency section (which focuses on context reduction techniques, not operation-level budgeting). Community validation is low (40): community project with mystical terminology, no star count surfaced in discovery, no official backing. Integration complexity is high if adopting the framework (50); lower if only extracting the charge management concept. Capability expansion is low overall (45) because majority is duplicate. Research needed: (1) Evaluate charge management pattern independently — is it worth extracting as a technique/playbook separate from Excalibur? (2) Check GitHub for star count and recent activity. (3) Compare charge management to any existing token-budget patterns in our library. If charge management is extracted as a standalone technique, that sub-item likely scores 70+.

partial_answers.library_charge_management_check: No existing library/techniques/ entry covers per-operation token budgeting. Charge management concept is novel relative to current library.
partial_answers.tiered_memory_overlap: Agent-event-bus + CLAUDE.md hierarchy covers this adequately. Excalibur's tiered memory adds nothing novel.
